arxiv-2202-08586.title: Collisional regime during the discharge of a 2D silo
arxiv-2202-08586.creator: Roberto Arévalo
arxiv-2202-08586.description: Abstract The present work reports a novel investigation into the collisional dynamics of particles in the vicinity of the outlet of a 2D silo using molecular dynamics simulations. Most studies on this granular system focus in the bulk of the medium.

arxiv-2202-10091.title: Control of protein-based pattern formation via guiding cues
arxiv-2202-10091.creator: Tom Burkart, Manon C. Wigbers, Laeschkir Würthner, Erwin Frey
arxiv-2202-10091.description: Abstract Proteins control many vital functions in living cells, such as cell growth and cell division. Reliable coordination of these functions requires the spatial and temporal organizaton of proteins inside cells, which encodes information about the cell’s geometry and the cell-cycle stage.

arxiv-2205-12120.title: Extended molt phenology models improve inferences about molt duration and timing
arxiv-2205-12120.creator: Philipp H. Boersch-Supan*, Hugh J. Hanmer & Robert A. Robinson
arxiv-2205-12120.description: Abstract 1 British Trust for Ornithology, The Nunnery, Thetford IP24 2PU, United Kingdom; * Corresponding author: pboesu@gmail.com Introduction All birds and most mammals rely on feathers and fur, respectively, to deliver critical functions such as thermoregulation (Wolf and Walsberg 2000, Dawson et al. 2014), social signaling and crypsis (Caro 2005, McQueen et al. 2019), or flight (Matloff et al. 2020).

arxiv-2210-17280.title: The compact-open topology on the homeomorphism group of a surface without boundary is minimal. Thanks: Work supported by Samsung Science and Technology Foundation under Project Number SSTF-BA1301-51.
arxiv-2210-17280.creator: J. de la Nuez González
arxiv-2210-17280.description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by J. de la Nuez González. We show that the homeomorphism group of a surface without boundary does not admit a Hausdorff group topology strictly coarser than the compact-open topology. In combination with known automatic continuity results, this implies that the compact-open topology is the unique Hausdorff separable group topology on the group if the surface is closed or the complement in a closed surface of either a finite set or the union of a finite set and a Cantor set.

arxiv-2302-01342.title: Curriculum-Guided Abstractive Summarization
arxiv-2302-01342.creator: Sajad Sotudeh, Hanieh Deilamsalehy, Franck Dernoncourt, Nazli Goharian
arxiv-2302-01342.description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Sajad Sotudeh, Hanieh Deilamsalehy, Franck Dernoncourt, Nazli Goharian. Recent Transformer-based summarization models have provided a promising approach to abstractive summarization. They go beyond sentence selection and extractive strategies to deal with more complicated tasks such as novel word generation and sentence paraphrasing. Nonetheless, these models have two shortcomings: (1) they often perform poorly in content selection, and (2) their training strategy is not quite efficient, which restricts model performance. In this paper, we explore two orthogonal ways to compensate for these pitfalls.

arxiv-2308-07171.title: Small sets of genuinely nonlocal GHZ states in multipartite systems
arxiv-2308-07171.creator: Zong-Xing Xiong 1 , Yongli Zhang 2 , Mao-Sheng Li 3 , Lvzhou Li 1 1 Institute of Quantum Computing and Software, School of Computer Science and Engineering, Sun Yat-Sen University, Guangzhou 510006, China 2 School of Mathematics and Systems Science, Guangdong Polytechnic Normal University, Guangzhou
arxiv-2308-07171.description: Abstract A set of orthogonal multipartite quantum states are called (distinguishability-based) genuinely nonlocal if they are locally indistinguishable across any bipartition of the subsystems. In this work, we consider the problem of constructing small genuinely nonlocal sets consisting of generalized GHZ states in multipartite systems.

arxiv-2406-01547.creator: Kalyan Dasgupta
arxiv-2406-01547.description: Abstract 1 Introduction Lattice models or structures are geometrical objects with mathematical forms, that are used to represent physical systems. They have been used widely in diverse fields, namely, in condensed matter physics, to study degrees of freedom of molecules in chemistry and in studying polymer dynamics and protein structures to name a few [ 1 ] .

arxiv-2406-09653.title: An alternate approach for estimating grain-growth kinetics
arxiv-2406-09653.creator: M Prabhakar, P G Kubendran Amos
arxiv-2406-09653.description: Abstract Rate of grain growth, which aides in achieving desired properties in polycrystalline materials, is conventionally estimated by measuring the size of grains and tracking its change in micrographs reflecting the temporal evolution. Techniques adopting this conventional approach demand an absolute distinction between the grains and the interface separating them to yield an accurate result.

arxiv-2502-00732.title: On cyclic group covers of the projective line
arxiv-2502-00732.creator: George Katsimprakis, Aristides Kontogeorgis
arxiv-2502-00732.description: Abstract . This article extends the study of cyclic ramified covers of the projective line defined by Kummer equations. We consider the most general case of such covers, allowing arbitrary orders in the roots of the generating radicant. The primary goal is the computation of the fundamental group of both the open and complete curve.

arxiv-2503-18167.title: Evaluating Negative Sampling Approaches for Neural Topic Models
arxiv-2503-18167.creator: Suman Adhya, Avishek Lahiri, Debarshi Kumar Sanyal, Partha Pratim Das
arxiv-2503-18167.description: Abstract Negative sampling has emerged as an effective technique that enables deep learning models to learn better representations by introducing the paradigm of “learn-to-compare”. The goal of this approach is to add robustness to deep learning models to learn better representation by comparing the positive samples against the negative ones.

pmc-10482081.title: Hinge Strut: A New Septal Strut for Nasal Tip Projection, Definition, and Stability in Latino Noses
pmc-10482081.creator: Wilder A. Pérez Willis, Gerardo A. Adrianzen Nuñez, Cynthia P. Mendoza Guerra, Wilder A. Perez Soto
pmc-10482081.description: Background:Obtaining ideal support to maintain the nasal tip has been investigated in several rhinoplasty studies. We aimed to describe a support technique, namely the use of a “hinge strut” (HS) for the nasal tip in Latino noses and to evaluate nasolabial angles at 6-months follow-up.

pmc-11485236.title: Single-neuron representations of odours in the human brain
pmc-11485236.creator: Marcel S. Kehl, Sina Mackay, Kathrin Ohla, Matthias Schneider, Valeri Borger, Rainer Surges, Marc Spehr, Florian Mormann
pmc-11485236.description: Olfaction is a fundamental sensory modality that guides animal and human behaviour1,2. However, the underlying neural processes of human olfaction are still poorly understood at the fundamental—that is, the single-neuron—level. Here we report recordings of single-neuron activity in the piriform cortex and medial temporal lobe in awake humans performing an odour rating and identification task.

pmc-11543202.title: Risk of second primary cancers in nodal non-Hodgkin lymphoma patients by primary lymph node location: a retrospective cohort population-based study
pmc-11543202.creator: Ali Hemade, Souheil Hallit
pmc-11543202.description: Background:Non-Hodgkin lymphoma (NHL) is a diverse group of blood cancers with increasing incidence and survival rates due to advancements in treatment and early detection. However, NHL survivors are at significant risk of developing second primary cancers, which can adversely impact their long-term survival.

pmc-11596253.title: Exopolysaccharide-Producing Bacteria Regulate Soil Aggregates and Bacterial Communities to Inhibit the Uptake of Cadmium and Lead by Lettuce
pmc-11596253.creator: Heyun Zhang, Ke Wang, Xinru Liu, Lunguang Yao, Zhaojin Chen, Hui Han, Juan Carlos Gutiérrez
pmc-11596253.description: The accumulation of heavy metals in the soil not only causes serious damage to the soil ecosystem, but also threatens human health through the food chain. Exopolysaccharides have the functions of adsorbing and chelating heavy metals and reducing their bioavailability in the soil.

pmc-12428407.title: The Emerging Role of the Brain–Gut Axis in Amyotrophic Lateral Sclerosis: Pathogenesis, Mechanisms, and Therapeutic Perspectives
pmc-12428407.creator: Eun Jin Yang, Fabrizio Michetti
pmc-12428407.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). Amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (ALS) is a fatal neurodegenerative disease characterized by progressive loss of motor neurons. Although genetic and environmental factors are established contributors, recent research has highlighted the critical role of the gut–brain axis (GBA) in ALS pathogenesis. The GBA is a bidirectional communication network involving neural, immune, and endocrine pathways that connect the gut microbiota with the central nervous system. Dysbiosis in ALS disrupts this axis, leading to increased intestinal permeability, neuroinflammation, and excitotoxicity.

pmc-12513158.title: Transcriptome-based meta-analysis of drought stress regulatory genes in tomato
pmc-12513158.creator: Maryam Murtaza, Muhammad Aqeel, Saad Abdulmageed Waheeb, Nazia Rehman, Samra Irum, Hanan Almahasheer, Rawabi Zahed, Reem Nabil Hassan, Sajid Fiaz, Muhammad Uzair, Muhammad Ramzan Khan, Ghulam Muhammad Ali, Mariusz Jaremko
pmc-12513158.description: Plants possess various molecular defense systems to ward off biotic and abiotic stresses and adjust to environmental changes. The RNA-seq technology assists biologists in quickly identifying genes responding to abiotic stresses. Thereby, using meta-transcriptomic data from the GEO NCBI public database, we have attempted to reach a consensus on gene variations.

pmc-12745685.title: Body ownership gates tactile awareness by reshaping the somatosensory functional connectivity
pmc-12745685.creator: Alberto Pisoni, Carlotta Fossataro, Alice Rossi Sebastiano, Marcella Romeo, Eleonora Arrigoni, Leonor Josefina Romero Lauro, Nadia Bolognini, Francesca Garbarini
pmc-12745685.description: We all likely agree that tactile experience contributes to the emergence of the feeling of ownership over one’s own body. Is the opposite true? We answered this question by testing whether and how the sense of body ownership gates our tactile experience.

pmc-13104524.title: A decade of Streptococcus pneumoniae bloodstream infections: a single-center retrospective analysis
pmc-13104524.creator: Saied Ali, Karen Burns, Binu Dinesh, Helene McDermott, Sinead O’Donnell, Fidelma Fitzpatrick, Ciara O’Connor
pmc-13104524.description: A ten-year retrospective review of 176 pneumococcal bloodstream infections found broad-spectrum antimicrobial use despite high penicillin susceptibility. Complications occurred in 15%, and ICU admission in 10%. Only 22% had pneumococcal vaccination recommended at discharge. Findings reveal missed opportunities for Antimicrobial Stewardship and preventative care in invasive pneumococcal disease management.
